title: Topologically protected perfect crossed Andreev reflection in flux-engineered quantum wire junctions
abstract: Generating non-locally entangled electron pairs via Cooper-pair splitting is vital for solid-state quantum information processing. However, isolating the underlying crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) is challenging due to competing transport processes like electron tunneling (ET) and local Andreev reflection (AR). Here, we propose a flux-tunable four-terminal normal metal-superconductor junction that achieves deterministic, 100\% efficient CAR. We demonstrate that at exactly half a magnetic flux quantum ($φ=π$), exact destructive Aharonov-Bohm and Peierls interferences structurally forbid ET and AR respectively. By tuning the central junction hopping, electron reflection is also suppressed to zero. Using the Cauchy argument principle, we prove that this suppression manifests as a quantized topological winding number, guaranteeing a topologically protected unit CAR probability. We establish that this regime is characterized by a strictly positive cross-correlation shot noise, providing an unambiguous experimental signature of Cooper-pair splitting. Furthermore, this perfect CAR is nearly broadband within the superconducting gap and remarkably robust against structural disorder, offering a highly resilient architecture for deterministic nonlocal entanglement generation.
summary: This work proposes a novel, flux-tunable quantum junction architecture that achieves perfect Crossed Andreev Reflection (CAR) by engineering destructive quantum interferences at $\phi=\pi$. The authors use topological theory and cross-correlation shot noise measurements to prove that this perfect, non-local entanglement generation is robust and fundamentally protected against disorder.
main_problem: The core challenge is to isolate and deterministically generate non-locally entangled electron pairs via Crossed Andreev Reflection (CAR) in solid-state systems, separating it from competing processes like electron tunneling (ET) and local Andreev reflection (AR).
main_result: The authors demonstrate that at exactly half a magnetic flux quantum ($\phi = \pi$), a specific flux-tunable junction achieves 100% efficient, topologically protected CAR, confirmed by a strictly positive cross-correlation shot noise signature.
method: The analysis combines theoretical modeling using a tight-binding Hamiltonian with advanced mathematical tools, specifically the Cauchy argument principle, to prove topological protection.
model_or_system: The system is a flux-tunable four-terminal normal metal-superconductor junction, modeled by a central square lattice threaded by a magnetic flux $\phi$. The Hamiltonian describes hopping amplitudes and superconducting pairing.
key_observables: Nonlocal differential conductance ($G_{RL}$), cross-correlation shot noise ($S_{13}$), and the topological winding number ($W$).
important_parameters: The critical flux value $\phi = \pi$, the superconducting gap ($\Delta$), and the ratio of hopping amplitudes ($t'/t$).
main_assumptions: The proof relies on the Cauchy argument principle to guarantee the topological protection of the perfect CAR state, and the analysis assumes the system can be modeled by a tight-binding lattice.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mechanism of interference suppression at $\phi=\pi$, show the quantized topological winding number ($W=1$), and confirm the unique positive cross-correlation shot noise signature ($S_{13}$) at this flux.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical problem and the Hamiltonian. It then calculates key observables like $G_{RL}$ and $S_{13}$. The core of the work uses topological arguments (Cauchy principle) to prove the existence of perfect CAR, followed by demonstrating its robustness against disorder.
why_interesting: The use of topological invariants (winding number) to guarantee a physical transport property (perfect CAR) provides a powerful, robust design principle for quantum devices, which is highly relevant to open quantum systems engineering.

FIG. 2. Giant enhancement of crossed Andreev reflection. (a) The logarithmic nonlocal conductance, η = log[1 + GRLh/(2e2)], versus magnetic flux ϕ at zero bias for various junction hoppings t′/t (shown in the legend). (b) Dependence of η on bias voltage V and hopping t′ at ϕ = π. Parameters are µ = −t, ∆= 0.01t, and ϵ0 = 0.6∆.

FIG. 4. Cross-correlation shot noise S13 between the nor- mal terminals as a function of the applied flux ϕ at a small bias voltage V near zero energy for various hopping ratios t′/t. The strictly positive noise near ϕ = π (green shaded region) is a feature of CAR-dominated Cooper-pair splitting. Notably, for the optimal hopping t′ = 0.7051t, the noise vanishes com- pletely at ϕ = π, reflecting the deterministic, fluctuation-free nature of perfect CAR (PCAR = 1). Conversely, the brown shaded regions denote the ET-dominated regime. Parameters are the same as in Fig. 2.

FIG. 3. Topological protection of perfect CAR. (a) Map of η versus ϵ0 and t′ at zero bias. The phase winding of the electron reflection (ER) amplitude along the indicated closed loop yields W = 1, topologically guaranteeing a zero of ER (perfect CAR) within the enclosed region. (b) Trajectory of the perfect CAR condition in the (E, ϵ0, t′) parameter space. Other parameters are the same as in Fig. 2.

FIG. 5. Robustness of CAR-dominated non-local conduc- tance under structural and chemical potential fluctuations. (a,b) Bond disorder with hoppings in the range [t′ −δt′/2, t′ + δt′/2]. (a) Bias dependence of GRL at fixed bond disorder amplitude δt′ = 0.2t near t′ = 0.706t. (b) GRL versus bond disorder strength δt′ at zero bias.
